# TASK-250: Make capped watched-root scans converge safely

## Metadata

- Kind: `implementation`
- Level: `3`
- Wave: `6`
- Workstream: `evidence-coverage`
- Selection: `primary`
- Execution: `implemented`

## Goal

Replace repeated first-page partial scans with durable bounded scan generations that eventually cover each configured root, preserve uncertainty between slices, and reconcile changes only when a generation completes.

## Deliverables

- Durable scan-generation persistence
- Bounded resumable traversal
- Atomic complete-generation reconciliation
- Coverage-progress diagnostics
- Restart and multi-slice tests

## Allowed Write Scope

- Sources/DiskStewardCore/Monitoring/**
- Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/**
- Sources/DiskStewardApp/Lifecycle/**

- Tests/DiskStewardCoreTests/Monitoring/**
- Tests/DiskStewardCoreTests/EvidenceStore/**
- Tests/DiskStewardAppTests/EvidenceState/**
- docs/tasks/evidence/TASK-250/**

## Non-Goals

- Scanning file contents
- Treating one capped slice as complete
- Automatically adding roots without user configuration or permission

- CONTRACT-250 deliverables
- TASK-241 reconciler and current-state projection

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-250-01` — Each capped work slice persists a generation identifier, root cursor or equivalent deterministic frontier, observed object staging, counts, timestamps, limitations, and restart-safe progress without mutating authoritative current state from incomplete absence.
- `AC-250-02` — Repeated bounded runs over a root larger than the per-slice cap eventually finish one complete generation, atomically reconcile the full object set, close the entry-cap gap, and permit subsequent complete generations to produce create, modify, rename, truncate, replace, and delete evidence.
- `AC-250-03` — Restart resumes valid progress; a scope-version change or invalid cursor abandons the old generation with explicit coverage evidence and starts a new generation without fabricating deletion.
- `AC-250-04` — Status and query models disclose configured roots, exclusions, current generation progress, last complete generation time, and whether current state is stale, partial, or complete.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-250-01` (convergent-scan-test) — A small-cap fixture requires multiple slices, survives restart, changes scope safely, completes with no duplicates, then proves a second generation detects A/B/C deletion only after full coverage.
